blocks.text: Turkmenistan is divided into five provinces, *welaýatlar*, and the capital, Ashgabat, which is run as a province of its own. Between them they cover land from the Caspian Sea to the Amu Darya, and most of it is desert: the Karakum fills the middle of the country, and together with the dry west it makes up about nine-tenths of the territory.

**Ahal** lies along the foot of the Kopetdag mountains in the south and surrounds Ashgabat. Its oases gave their name to the Akhal-Teke horse of [A1 unit 2](a1-u02-culture). In the early 2020s the province was given a newly built administrative centre.

**Balkan**, in the west, is the largest province, about 139,000 square kilometres, and the most thinly peopled. It runs along the Caspian coast, with the port of Türkmenbaşy and the towns of Hazar and Esenguly, the home of *küştdepdi*. Its centre is Balkanabat. One scholar, the historian Barthold, believed the name Balkan comes from a Persian word for **upper house**; it is one view, not a settled fact.

**Daşoguz** is the north, on the lower Amu Darya towards the Aral Sea. **Lebap** is the east, along the middle course of the same river; its name comes from the Persian **lab-e âb**, **riverside**, and its centre is Türkmenabat, the country's second city. **Mary**, in the south-east, is the oasis of the Murgab river, with the town of Mary, ancient Merv of [A2 unit 3](a2-u03-culture), and Gonur Depe of the next unit. At the 2022 census it was the most populous province, with about 1.6 million people; Balkan had about 530,000, and Ashgabat just over a million.

The climate is continental: on average 14 to 16 °C over the year, but summer days rarely fall below 35 °C, the south-east Karakum has reached 50 °C, and winter nights in the far south have gone down to −33 °C.

blocks.tk: Jeýhun bilen bahry-Hazar arasy, / Çöl üstünden öwser ýeli türkmeniň.
blocks.en: Between the Jeyhun and the Caspian Sea, / over the desert blows the Turkmen's wind.

blocks.text: Magtymguly, the poet of the eighteenth century, drew the same map in two lines: the Jeyhun is the old name of the Amu Darya, and *bahry-Hazar* the Caspian Sea. You will meet *arasy*, **between**, and *üstünden*, **over**, in the next unit.
With this unit's comparatives, you can read this:

blocks.tk: Türkmenistanda bäş welaýat bar: Ahal, Balkan, Daşoguz, Lebap we Mary. Balkan iň uly welaýat, ýöne onda adam az. Mary Balkandan kiçi, ýöne onda adam köp. Daşoguz demirgazykda, Lebap gündogarda. Paýtagt Aşgabat hem welaýat ýaly.
blocks.en: There are five provinces in Turkmenistan: Ahal, Balkan, Daşoguz, Lebap and Mary. Balkan is the biggest province, but few people live there. Mary is smaller than Balkan, but many people live there. Daşoguz is in the north, Lebap in the east. The capital, Ashgabat, is like a province too.

questions.explain: *Balkan iň uly welaýat*: the largest, and the most thinly peopled.

questions.q: What does the name Lebap mean?
questions.explain: From the Persian **lab-e âb**, **riverside**: the province follows the Amu Darya.

questions.q: In the reading, where do many people live?
questions.explain: *Mary Balkandan kiçi, ýöne onda adam köp*: smaller than Balkan, but with many people.

sources.title: Regions of Turkmenistan
sources.note: Five welaýats and Ashgabat, with areas and 2022 census populations (Balkan 139,300 km², 529,895; Mary 1,613,386; Ashgabat 1,030,063); a 2022 decree on a new administrative centre for Ahal

sources.title: Balkan Region
sources.note: The westernmost region, on the Caspian; capital Balkanabat; lowest population density; Türkmenbaşy, Hazar, Esenguly; Barthold's derivation of the name from Persian bālākhāna, upper house

sources.title: Lebap Region
sources.note: The name from Persian lab-e âb, riverside; along the Amu Darya; centre Türkmenabat

sources.title: Türkmenabat
sources.note: The second-largest city in Turkmenistan and the centre of Lebap Province, formerly Çärjew

sources.title: Turkmenistan
sources.note: The desert region nine-tenths of the territory; the Kopet-Dag in the south; the Amu Darya on the north-east border; the Morghab oasis around Mary; average annual temperature 14–16 °C, summer days rarely below 35 °C, 50 °C in the south-east Karakum, −33 °C at Serhetabat

sources.title: Turkmen language
